text: `fib(n-1) + fib(n-2)` is tree recursion and `fact(n-1)` is linear recursion. What distinguishes them?
choices: The number of recursive calls per level — one call gives a chain, two give a branching tree whose size grows exponentially.
Tree recursion requires memoisation to terminate; linear recursion terminates on its own.
Tree recursion returns a value while linear recursion accumulates into a parameter.
Tree recursion uses more stack, since each level holds two frames simultaneously.
explanation: Two calls per level means 2^n nodes in the worst case, which is why Fibonacci is expensive and factorial is not. The last distractor is a common misreading: the two calls happen one after the other, so the *depth* is still linear and only the *count* is exponential — the program runs out of time long before it runs out of stack.
